chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who was struck on his head, so his hearing and sight went away and his tongue became impaired, then he died. He said: “If he struck him blow after blow, qiṣāṣ is taken from him, then he is killed. But if this befell him from a single blow, he is killed and qiṣāṣ is not taken from him.”

key_terms.لِسَانُهُ: his tongue, meaning his speech faculty

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person causes loss of hearing, sight, speech, and then death through one blow or multiple blows?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding qiṣāṣ when a victim suffers multiple severe injuries and then dies from an assault. It distinguishes between repeated blows, for which retaliatory punishment is taken before execution, and a single blow causing all the harm, for which only execution is carried out.
